readme_snippet: Reading query plans Run it correctly ANALYZE executes the query. For UPDATE or DELETE, wrap it in a transaction and roll back. BUFFERS is the commonly omitted flag that matters most: it shows how much data was actually touched. SETTINGS shows non-default planner parameters, which explains environment differences. Start with estimate versus actual A plan is a set of decisions built on estimates. When an estimate is off by 40,000x, every decision above it in the tree rests on a wrong assumption: join strategy, memory allocation, index choice. Fixing the estimate usually fixes the query without touching the SQL. Read the plan bottom-up and find the deepest node where estimate and actual differ by more than about 10x. That node is the root cause. Everything above it is a symptom. Fixing bad estimates | Cause | Fix | |---|---| | Stale statistics | ANALYZE tablename;.

readme_snippet: Resolving Flutter Layout Errors Contents Constraint Violation Diagnostics Layout Error Resolution Workflow Examples Constraint Violation Diagnostics Flutter layout operates on a strict rule: Constraints go down. Sizes go up. Parent sets position. Layout errors occur when this negotiation fails, typically due to unbounded constraints or unconstrained children. Diagnose layout failures using the following error signatures: "Vertical viewport was given unbounded height": Triggered when a scrollable widget (ListView, GridView) is placed inside an unconstrained vertical parent (Column). The parent provides infinite height, and the child attempts to expand infinitely. "An InputDecorator...cannot have an unbounded width": Triggered when a TextField or TextFormField is placed inside an unconstrained horizontal parent (Row). The text field attempts to determine its width based on infinite available space.
